chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Hadeed, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When the Night Journey was made for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he rose in the morning, sat down, and narrated it to them. They said to him, 'Describe for us Al-Bait Al-Maqdis.' So he described it to them, but he had entered it at night, so the description became vague/confused for him. Then Jibraeel (peace be upon him) came to him and said, 'Look here!' So he looked towards the House (Al-Maqdis) and described it while looking at it. Then he described to them the caravan that was between them and Syria. Then he said, 'This is the caravan of the clan of so-and-so, arriving with the rising of the sun, preceded by a red or white camel.' He said, 'And the Quraysh sent a man on a horse to turn it back.' He said, 'And it arrived with the rising of the sun.' Qurtat ibn Abd Amr said, 'O grief that I am not a trunk (strong support) for you when you claim that you came to Al-Bait Al-Maqdis and returned in the same night.'
ai.seo_question: How did the Prophet Muhammad describe Al-Bait Al-Maqdis during the Night Journey?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Kafi elucidates the physical reality of the Isra by detailing how the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) relied on Jibraeel’s guidance to accurately describe Al-Bait Al-Maqdis despite the brevity of his nocturnal visit. It further establishes the veracity of the Prophet’s claim through the miraculous sign of the caravan, a specific event known to the Quraysh, thereby serving as a tangible proof (burhan) for the Meccan polytheists. This account underscores the Shia emphasis on the literal nature of the Night Journey and its role in validating prophetic authority through observable miracles.
